nodes.label: Store incident planning data as Mission Properties
nodes.rationale: Planning data lived in one mission_schema.json on the management DataSync, re-uploaded whole on every save, so two managers silently overwrote each other even on unrelated sections. TAK Server 5.9 Mission Properties are per-key atomic upserts that follow mission group rules (still hidden from field users) and announce t-x-m-c-p, but they are not kept in the mission change history. Anything that needs an audit trail, such as published CAD notes or POA locks, must record it in its own keys. Production waits on AZTAK's 5.9 upgrade; older servers keep the file. Upstream support is node-tak #44, CloudTAK #1852, node-cot #143, and CloudTAK #1919.

nodes.label: mission_schema.json
nodes.rationale: The previous single-file store on the MGMT DataSync. Kept unchanged for servers without Mission Properties, and for incidents that have not been moved.

nodes.label: Mission Property layout v3
nodes.rationale: One key per independently edited piece, implemented in schemaCodec.ts and schemaCollections.ts: meta.schema (currently 3), s.<field> and s.incident-response.<field>, op.<n>.mission, op.<n>.debrief.<segment>.<id>, and c.<collection>.<id> for segments, ROW segments, resources, work assignments, op assignments, clues, CAD notes, and each IAP field per OP. Values without a safe unique key stay inside the field's s. key. Keys are limited to [A-Za-z0-9.:-] because the server prefix filter is SQL LIKE, where _ and % are wildcards, and / breaks the URL path, so schema names use - instead of _. Layout v2, one key per schema field, was superseded because two people adding different segments, resources, or CAD notes still wrote the same key.

nodes.label: SchemaConflictError
nodes.rationale: Saves are diffs against the loaded copy, at most 8 keys at a time. Before writing, each changed key is checked on the server; if another manager changed it since load, the save stops with SchemaConflictError, writes nothing, and asks for a reload. Same-record edits stay exclusive; different records never collide. IAP updated-timestamp keys are exempt via isVolatileKey. Open screens re-list every 15s while visible; after a CloudTAK #1919 push is seen, polling drops to 60s. Lists refresh themselves; forms show a Reload banner and never reload over in-progress typing. A tab's own writes are filtered out.

nodes.label: Layout upgrade on first save
nodes.rationale: Upgrades run on the first save after a new layout ships, never on load, because load may have no write token: the incident is re-encoded, the difference is written, and meta.schema is bumped last. A first upgrade can write 100+ keys (FLORES about 150). An older plugin cannot read layout-3 collection records, so every CloudTAK instance on one TAK Server must run the same plugin build. New incidents start on properties when the server supports them; existing ones move from the Dashboard by reading back and comparing key by key.

nodes.label: MGMT DataSync
nodes.rationale: Each incident has a management DataSync that only management channels can see. Planning properties are stored there so they stay as hidden from field users as mission_schema.json was.

nodes.label: File locking or JSON merge alternative
nodes.rationale: Keeping mission_schema.json would work on every TAK Server version, but TAK has no conditional upload, so any lock would be advisory and client-side, and merging whole-file JSON from several writers is error-prone. Rejected because it does not remove the overwrite problem.

nodes.label: CloudTAK Events as data store
nodes.rationale: CloudTAK 13.107.3 Events can hold several DataSyncs in missions[]. Not chosen: the intended direction is Events that group DataSyncs, not Events as a per-OP data store, and Events do not inherit TAK group visibility the way MGMT DataSync properties do. Grouping an incident's OP DataSyncs under an Event remains a planned follow-up.

nodes.label: Layout v2 one key per schema field
nodes.rationale: Simple and it solved most cross-section overwrites, but two people adding different segments, resources, or CAD notes still wrote the same key. Superseded by per-record collection keys in layout v3.
